classification: Fictional loopback experiment with real walt.id v2 and two real WordPress pages; no human wallet use or HTTPS deployment

checks.name: Real walt.id credential links only after same-browser confirmation.
Opted-in WordPress admits wallet membership; ordinary WordPress receives hosted membership only and still opens its page.
Operator enablement and website request are both required; either alone leaves hosted access intact.
Two real WordPress member pages accept separately consented identities with different subjects.
Disabling operator capability removes wallet access on an existing session.
Withdrawing wallet sharing closes only the selected website; ordinary sign-in remains.
Organisation revocation closes actual protected pages within 5 s refresh plus 1 s test tolerance.
Replacing the credential and wallet key preserves both WordPress accounts.
Status outage closes actual member pages within 20 s plus 1 s test tolerance; native administrator access remains.
PHP ignores a valid unaccepted wallet statement while retaining unrelated hosted membership.
A member without a wallet signs in normally without gaining unapproved member access.

components.credential: dc+sd-jwt (SD-JWT VC), ES256, holder key binding (cnf.jwk), IETF Token Status List reference
components.verifier: Unanym src/wallet (this branch): OpenID4VP direct_post, redirect_uri client identifier, SD-JWT + KB-JWT verification, status list signature/subject/freshness

limitations: Fictional organisations and accounts; no real-member acceptance
Wallet API v2, not a person using a phone wallet
Loopback HTTP only; no HTTPS deployment
Same-browser completion only; other wallets and cross-device completion untested
Operator can correlate accounts and presentations
